summary: Iteration 3 - Teacher Portal 'Digital Classroom' end-to-end testing. Added /app/backend/tests/test_classroom.py with 24 tests covering: teacher dashboard fields (my_classes/students/homework/materials/videos/subjects/school_name/recent_homework), /classroom/my-classes scoped to assigned classes only (excludes unassigned + cross-school), homework CRUD with 403 on unassigned/cross-school create, student & parent read-only visibility scoped to own class, cross-school hide + 403 on cross-school delete, teacher can only delete own items, student cannot create/delete, file upload (PDF) + material create + authenticated download via /api/files (cookie/header/query all supported), video CRUD with same isolation, attendance regression for teacher assigned/unassigned + persistence, logout clears session, teacher cannot change own role. Result: 24/24 PASS. Combined regression 84/84 (backend_test 32 + founder_portal 28 + classroom 24) in 33.6s. Frontend Playwright smoke: teacher login auto-routes to TeacherDashboard (all 6 stat cards, quick-actions grid, welcome+school name+subject chips, recent homework); My Classes shows only assigned class with section + student count + subjects; Homework/Videos create flows work end-to-end via modals with data-testids; created items visible in list and persist after page refresh.

issues: Radix DialogContent missing Description/aria-describedby - a11y warning (console)

action_items: Optional: add DialogDescription (or aria-describedby) to Homework/Material/Video/Confirm dialogs to silence Radix a11y warnings.
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED (I applied): /api/upload previously rejected .pdf even though frontend accept='.pdf,...' and spec says 'PDF/image file'. Added 'pdf' to ALLOWED_IMAGE_EXT in /app/backend/storage.py.

FIXED (I applied): /api/files/{path} download only read Authorization header or ?auth= query - it ignored the httpOnly access_token cookie. This broke plain <a href> downloads from Materials.jsx and Homework.jsx attachment links which rely on browser-sent cookies. Added cookie fallback in /app/backend/routes_files.py.

routes_classroom.read_query() correctly scopes by role: founder=all, teacher=assigned_classes, student=own class, parent=children class ids, school_admin/principal=whole school; and uses ['__none__'] sentinel to avoid empty-$in leaks - solid.
assert_can_create() correctly enforces teacher-assigned-class-only for POST /classroom/*.
Delete rule: teacher can only delete own item (teacher_id == self); students/parents blocked; cross-school blocked via assert_school_access -- covered by tests.
TeacherDashboard uses `my` filter = teacher_id which correctly counts only self-created items even if teacher moves classes.
MINOR: /api/upload MIME whitelist is thin (5 image types + pdf). Consider validating content-type against extension to prevent MIME spoofing (a client can rename .exe to .pdf and upload).

MINOR: routes_files.download uses raw jwt.decode - it does not verify token 'type' == access or the user's token_version. A stale/refresh/tampered access token could still fetch files. Consider reusing get_current_user semantics.
MINOR: /classroom/my-classes iterates assigned_classes with per-class count_documents (O(N)); acceptable for typical teacher load (<10 classes).
MINOR: HomeworkInput/MaterialInput/VideoInput have no length caps on title/description; consider Pydantic max_length to prevent abuse.

MINOR: Homework fileUrl in frontend is `${baseURL}/files/${p}` - works now that cookie auth is supported. Otherwise the <a> tag download would need ?auth=<token> which is not available with httpOnly cookies.

rca of the issue: Two backend integration bugs found & fixed this iteration: (1) PDF upload blocked - ALLOWED_IMAGE_EXT set omitted 'pdf' although MIME_TYPES already mapped 'pdf'->'application/pdf' and both material and homework frontend forms accept .pdf. Repro: POST /api/upload with a .pdf file -> 400 'Only image files ... are allowed'. Mitigation: added 'pdf' to ALLOWED_IMAGE_EXT in storage.py. (2) File download 401 for browser <a href> - the /api/files/{path} handler only inspected Authorization header and ?auth= query and did not fall back to the httpOnly access_token cookie. Since the frontend uses <a href={baseURL}/files/${path}> for attachment/material downloads, browsers send cookies automatically but the endpoint ignored them, returning 401. Mitigation: added `else: token = request.cookies.get('access_token')` fallback in routes_files.py.
